title: The Messy Sales Report

storyline.headline: Nova Electronics cannot trust its investor sales report
storyline.summary: Last month's export contains missing values, inconsistent labels, duplicate records, and formatting issues. Management needs a clean, credible summary before meeting investors.

objectives: Assess, clean, and summarise the sales evidence so management can trust the investor report.
starterCode: # Assess the quality of Nova's sales evidence
hints: Start by checking the structure and quality of every file before changing it.
Keep a clear distinction between the source file and your cleaned analytical view.
businessInsight: The source export contains duplicated transactions and incomplete store information, which would overstate sales and misattribute performance if left unresolved.
recommendation: Introduce required-field validation at export, enforce a single store naming standard, and add a duplicate transaction check before every investor reporting cycle.
businessQuestion: Can Nova Electronics rely on last month's sales data for its investor presentation?
strategy: Identify missing, inconsistent, duplicated, and incorrectly formatted information.
Recommend process controls to prevent recurrence.

handbook.heading: Checking data quality
handbook.whatItDoes: Analysts quantify missing information and inspect labels before cleaning anything.
handbook.useCase: Use it to understand whether a report is fit for purpose.

handbook.heading: Handling missing information
handbook.whatItDoes: A deliberate decision is needed: retain, replace, or exclude incomplete records.
handbook.useCase: Use it when a missing field makes a record unusable for the question.

handbook.heading: Summarising results
handbook.whatItDoes: A concise summary turns a clean dataset into a management-ready view.
handbook.useCase: Use it to communicate scale and variation without exposing every row.
